qt: to the Commission Alessandro Zan (S&D), Cecilia Strada (S&D), Lucia Annunziata (S&D), Brando Benifei (S&D), Stefano Bonaccini (S&D), Annalisa Corrado (S&D), Giorgio Gori (S&D), Elisabetta Gualmini (S&D), Camilla Laureti (S&D), Giuseppe Lupo (S&D), Pierfrancesco Maran (S&D), Alessandra Moretti (S&D), Dario Nardella (S&D), Pina Picierno (S&D), Matteo Ricci (S&D), Sandro Ruotolo (S&D), Marco Tarquinio (S&D), Irene Tinagli (S&D), Raffaele Topo (S&D), Nicola Zingaretti (S&D), Cristina Guarda (Verts/ALE), Benedetta Scuderi (Verts/ALE), Leoluca Orlando (Verts/ALE), Ignazio Roberto Marino (Verts/ALE), Ilaria Salis (The Left), Mimmo Lucano (The Left), Pasquale Tridico (The Left), Carolina Morace (The Left), Mario Furore (The Left), Gaetano Pedulla' (The Left) Subject:

Italian Decree Law No 158/20241 (and amendment 12.09 to draft bill no 20882) identifies a number of safe countries of origin in the Italian legal system. According to the country profiles attached to Inter-ministerial Decree No 105 of 7 May 2024, in some of the countries recognised as safe countries of origin, there are widely confirmed cases of acts of persecution and/or serious harm in specific parts of the territory or against clearly identifiable categories of person. In the light of the provisions of the Geneva Convention, Articles 2, 3 and 4 of the European Convention on Human Rights, the criteria for designating safe countries of origin as laid down in Directive 2013/32/EU – which all require the general and consistent absence of persecution and/or serious harm – and the judgment of the CJEU in Case C 406/22, can the Commission detail: 1.
whether the Italian list of safe countries of origin meets the criteria laid down in Directives 2011/95/EU and 2013/32/EU;

whether the fact that there are widely confirmed cases of acts of persecution and/or serious harm in countries designated as safe countries of origin should lead to those countries being taken off the national list of safe third countries;
in accordance with Article 37(2) of Directive 2013/32/EU, what its opinion is regarding a review?

at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (14.5.2025) The assessment of whether a third country meets the conditions set out in Annex I of Directive 2013/321 for the purpose of the designation as safe country of origin is conducted by Member States’ competent authorities, based on a range of sources of information. In any event, when the concept is applied in a procedure for international protection, an individual examination of the application submitted by applicants from designated safe countries of origin must always be carried out. Pursuant to Article 37(2) of Directive 2013/32, Member States must regularly review the situation in the designated safe countries of origin. This covers the occurrence of significant events which may affect the presumption that the concerned country can guarantee the safety of the applicant.
1 Directive 2013/32/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 26 June 2013 on common procedures
for granting and withdrawing international protection (recast) - OJ L 180, 29/06/2013, p. 60.
